experiments.name: Deep cryogenic treatment of quenched X210CrW12 (AISI D3-type) cold-work tool steel at -180 C for 12-36 h with 2 C/min cooling and heating, followed by 300 C tempering
experiments.plain_name: Deep-freeze a chromium cold-work tool steel at -180 C for up to a day and a half so it wears more slowly
experiments.description: Quenched X210CrW12 tool steel (austenitised 920 C, 25 min) is cooled at 2 C/min to -180 C, held 12, 18, 24 or 36 h, warmed at 2 C/min and tempered at 300 C for 2 h; hardness, tensile strength and pin-on-disc wear are compared with conventional quench-and-temper. The cryogenic device appears only as a schematic/photo (model not named).

requirements.rationale: The longest treatment of the series holds the steel at -180 C for 36 h, so the machine must sustain an uninterrupted 36 h soak.

experiments.name: Cryogenic comminution of whole passenger-car waste tyres: complete LN2 immersion (200-300 s, below Tg = 215 K) followed by a single pneumatic-hammer impact
experiments.plain_name: Freeze a whole scrap car tyre in liquid nitrogen until it turns glassy, then smash it into rubber crumb
experiments.description: One-piece waste passenger tyres (modelled as 185 mm wide, 75% profile, 13 inch landing diameter) are fully immersed in liquid nitrogen in a purpose-built vessel until intense boiling stops (200-300 s), taking the rubber below its 215 K glass transition, and are then shattered by an MA4129A pneumatic sledgehammer with profiled punches; crumb size distribution is reported.

requirements.rationale: The tyre is cooled by complete immersion in a liquid-nitrogen bath.

requirements.rationale: The rubber must be taken below its glass-transition temperature (215 K) so it shatters instead of deforming; the cooling medium must reach below 215 K.

requirements.quote: this temperature is the glass transition temperature, i.e., T g = 215 K

requirements.rationale: The whole tyre goes into the vessel; its 13 inch landing (rim) diameter is a lower bound on the clear diameter needed (the outer diameter, with the 75% x 185 mm sidewall on each side, is larger).

experiments.name: LN2 cold-shock test of cryogenic ground-support components (pipe spools, valves, filters, flex hoses): fill with LN2 until it exits, then cold-soak for at least 1 h (KSC-STD-Z-0009 Rev D 6.2.1)

experiments.description: After shop fabrication, cryogenic ground-support assemblies are cold-shock tested by introducing LN2 at the inlet until a steady LN2 stream exits, then maintaining the supply for a cold soak of at least 1 h; no deformation, leakage, frost or condensation on vacuum jackets is allowed, and annulus pressure is monitored until the assembly returns to ambient.

experiments.name: Vacuum-retention acceptance test of a vacuum-jacketed LN2 storage vessel: annulus evacuated to 50 microns or less, inner vessel filled and cooled with LN2, 48 h atmospheric hold then 1 h at MAWP (KSC-STD-Z-0009 Rev D 6.2.7)

notes: Web search (WebSearch budget) and Tavily quotas were exhausted during this run; sources were read with WebFetch, Europe PMC full text, local pdftotext of WebFetch-saved PDFs and the read-only built-in browser. No values were invented. LN2 mass flow (0.5 kg/min, Inconel paper) was not converted to L/min. Sample circumscribed diameters are exact arithmetic on the quoted dimensions, rounded up. CryoMill grinding and the Bombardier bushing PPS were not used: CryoMill duplicates existing rubber/chemistry cryomilling profiles and the PPS URL returned 404; ASTM D2137 gives no numeric conditions on its public page; the Ayed LN2 pressure/flow paper was 403.
